PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: prop-david-harp
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Prop/artifact guard: transfer only material response, patina, highlight rolloff, and photographic presentation. Do not add a glowing sword, sacred symbols, blood, or human hands unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
DAVID'S BROKEN HARP — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: HERO PROP DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, SCALE, AND CONTINUITY.

Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Hero production reference of King David's ancient portable harp from the biblical epic JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL, the sacred instrument of the psalmist-king carried still at his side when he is freed among the righteous in Hell's inner chamber—strings long broken, music silenced for ages, yet form intact as a vessel of restored hope. Complete freestanding object, fully visible and isolated for prop continuity, not cropped, not held by a figure in this plate unless only a faint soft-focus silhouette is needed for scale, primary focus always the harp alone.

Construction and silhouette: an Iron Age–period Near Eastern kinnor-style lyre-harp sized for an adult king's hands—soundbox roughly forearm-length, overall height about the span from hip to mid-chest when worn at the side, compact enough for centuries of captivity yet regal in proportion. Two upright arms rise from a hollow wooden sound chest and join at a gently curved yoke or crossbar; the arms are slightly asymmetric from age and stress, with a graceful classical biblical profile rather than a modern concert-harp shape. No pedals, no metal tuning machines of modern make, no piano-like body—only hand-carved ancient construction.

Materials: dense ancient hardwood soundbox—olive, cedar, or similar warm Mediterranean timber—deep honey-amber and black-brown grain darkened by millennia of handling, smoke, and subterranean damp. Wood shows hairline checks, soft edge wear where palms once gripped, and a satin-to-matte patina of oils, dust, and faint mineral grime from Hell's fortress air. The soundboard is thin and slightly concave, with a small circular or oval sound hole free of any lettering. Yoke and arms share the same aged timber; joins are wooden pegs and ancient hide-glue seams, some slightly open. Decorative metalwork is sparse and period-correct: thin hammered copper or low-gold bronze bands and rivets near the yoke ends and soundbox corners, heavily darkened, green-black verdigris in recesses, no chrome, no polished steel.

Strings and breakage state (critical continuity): originally multiple gut or sinew strings stretched from soundbox bridge to yoke; most are snapped, frayed, and hanging limp. Several broken ends still knotted or wound at the yoke with uneven tension; other remnants dangle from the bridge like torn spider silk; a few stubs remain as short stiff stubs near the hitch points. One or two strings may still span partially before a mid-span break, emphasizing centuries of silence rather than recent violence. No bright new nylon, no steel guitar wire, no modern frets.

Surface detail: low-relief carvings along the arms and soundbox edges—abstract vines, simple star motifs, interlocking geometric bands, and stylized olive-leaf patterns of ancient Israelite craftsmanship. All ornament is sculptural wood and metal only; no readable letters, no psalm verses, no Hebrew or Greek script, no monograms, no logos. Micro-scratches, thumb-polish on the most handled edges, fine ash-dust in carved channels, and a faint reddish-brown iron-oxide smear where the instrument once rested against corroded chain links or fortress stone.

Lighting and grade for liberation beat: soft warm amber key (~3200–4500K) with a gentle ethereal gold rim suggesting distant divine radiance entering Hell's inner chamber after the gate has fallen—warm amber and soft gold over residual cool blue torch spill in the far ambient only, never competing for the object's key. Subtle volumetric haze, fine dust motes, no harsh studio white. Color grade: honey wood tones, faded royal-blue and antique-gold flecks only if a thin worn leather or cloth strap remnant hangs from the instrument (deep blue-and-gold thread fabric frayed thin, matching David's faded royal garments continuity). Strap hardware simple bone or darkened bronze ring—no modern buckles.

Camera and presentation: neutral three-quarter product-hero angle slightly above eye level for props, 50–85mm equivalent, moderate depth of field so the full harp stays sharp while background falls into soft dark stone and soft blue-to-amber atmosphere. Aspect 2.39:1 cinematic framing acceptable; object centered with breathing room. Photoreal live-action biblical epic production reference—physically accurate wood grain, broken gut fiber, metal corrosion, no illustration, no CGI cartoon gloss, no fantasy neon, no modern objects. Continuity lock: same broken-string state as David's character prop—ancient wooden harp, strings broken, symbol of silenced then restored praise. No captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, no readable text of any kind on the instrument or in frame.
Neutral production reference framing, the complete object visible, accurate materials and scale, no labels or text.
